taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Many historical varieties are now treated as synonyms of the species; learner remains species-level.

evidence: Hays County — USDA-derived county distribution data record native Helenium autumnale in Hays County.
Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Asteraceae index includes Helenium autumnale; an additional wild Bull Creek record supports local occurrence.
Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed field-based county treatment.
USDA-derived county data additionally include Bell, Blanco, Gillespie and Kerr.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Cultivated garden sneezeweeds are common; PASS uses native county distribution/herbarium evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: First decide annual or perennial, then inspect the stem wings. Common/fall sneezeweed is the perennial in this batch, with stout strongly winged stems and much broader obovate-to-lanceolate leaves that are often toothed. Its flower heads are also substantially larger than bitterweed's tiny heads.
diagnostic_traits: perennial herb, often 50–130 cm in FNA though local plants may be shorter
stems strongly winged by broad decurrent leaf bases
mid-stem leaves obovate to oblanceolate/lanceolate, much broader than H. amarum or H. elegans
leaf margins often dentate or remotely toothed, sometimes entire distally
upper plant strongly branched with many heads
heads relatively large, involucres globoid about 8–20 mm in FNA
yellow rays commonly 8–21 and 10–23 mm long
typically late-summer to fall flowering and associated with moist roadsides, streams, ditches, seepage areas and pond margins

confusers.separator: H. amarum is an annual with unwinged stems, threadlike leaves and many tiny heads.
H. elegans is annual and narrow-leaved; H. autumnale is perennial with broader often toothed leaves and larger heads.
H. quadridentatum is annual with narrow entire distal leaves and 4-lobed disc corollas; H. autumnale is perennial and 5-lobed in the disc.

installation_guardrail: May install under the user's standing blanket approval because strict PASS is complete.
